result.summary: The street provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including continuous sidewalks and a marked crosswalk at the intersection. However, the environment lacks active traffic control or physical traffic calming measures, and parked vehicles along the curb may obstruct sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb block the line of sight between pedestrians and oncoming traffic at the crossing point.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No visible stop signs or signals at the marked crossing, which may lead to low driver yielding rates.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard crosswalk markings to a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility for approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Yield to Pedestrian' signage to alert drivers of the legal requirement to yield at the marked crossing.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow urban intersection with mixed-use buildings and basic pedestrian infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, the environment is characterized by faded crosswalk markings and sightline obstructions from parked vehicles near the corners.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings are significantly worn, making the pedestrian crossing area less visible to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the intersecting street

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are positioned very close to the intersection, blocking the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbsides near the intersection

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt in the roadway and near the crossing area may present tripping hazards or affect vehicle control.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines by preventing parking at the intersection.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides within a commercial corridor, but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. Parked vehicles along the curbs create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the two-lane roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous rows of parked cars on both sides of the street block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street length.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: In a commercial area with active storefronts, there are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations without priority.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility (continental style) crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and alert drivers to crossing locations.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic infrastructure such as sidewalks and a marked zebra crosswalk, but lacks active traffic control signals. Visibility is compromised by a large parked vehicle near the crossing, and the sidewalk is partially obstructed by debris and street furniture.

hazards.description: Debris and a trash can are placed in the middle of the pedestrian walkway, narrowing the accessible path.
